transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-15 16:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO - Aster Retail), Priya Sharma (Head of ML), Markus Li (Platform Eng)

Summary: Quick Console walkthrough focused on Usage Analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Covered token-level cost, per-route SLOs, routing and fallback policies, and security controls. Next steps: pricing, security docs, pilot setup.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Jordan (SE) and I will run through the Console, specifically the usage analytics and per-route dashboards and then jump into cost breakdowns. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Liam O'Connor: Good, thanks. Excited to see the console — we want to understand how we'd monitor costs across our different user-facing routes.
[00:20] Priya Sharma: Also want to see how per-route latency and token counts show up, and any ability to flag regressions.
[00:30] Maya Patel: Great. Quick agenda: overview of Console, usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns + Optimize recommendations, then Q&A and next steps. Jordan, kick us off on the dashboard.
[00:40] Jordan Lee: Cool. I'm in the Redwood Console now. Top nav, you can toggle between models, routes, and analytics. First screen is the Usage Analytics overview — shows total tokens, requests, avg latency, and a cost estimate. This is rolled up across chosen time windows.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Note: the token and cost numbers are estimates until you plug in your billing profile. We also show token distribution by route so you can see which routes are driving spend.
[01:20] Markus Li: Are those numbers per-second streaming or aggregated? We have a few bursty routes.
[01:28] Jordan Lee: Aggregated by default in the top-level. You can change granularity to 1m, 5m, 1h. For bursty routes we recommend the 1m view. There's also percentile latency to capture tail behavior.
[01:45] Priya Sharma: Is the token accounting broken down by input vs output tokens?
[01:50] Jordan Lee: Yes, the breakdown shows prompt tokens vs completion tokens. We also show model variant used per request — e.g., if you route to a quantized variant vs full fp16. There's sometimes transcription weirdness in the logs — you'll see it labeled as 'quant' or 'q8' etc.
[02:10] Liam O'Connor: Can we filter by model family? We run a mix of open models and want to compare.
[02:16] Jordan Lee: Yep, filter by model, region, deployment type (hosted vs dedicated), and tags you can set per route.
[02:26] Maya Patel: I'm going to open a per-route dashboard for the 'pricing-chat' route — this is a synthetic example.
[02:33] Jordan Lee: This per-route page shows time-series for requests/sec, avg latency, 95/99 latencies, token usage split, and a cost trend. The cost trend maps to unit economics: tokens * per-token-unit-cost + per-request overhead if you use function calling.
[02:50] Jordan Lee: We also surface anomaly detection flags — like sudden cost spike or higher completion token sizes — and link to sample requests.
[03:05] Priya Sharma: When it flags a sample request, can we see full input and output for debugging?
[03:10] Jordan Lee: Yes, if your retention policy allows. For hosted customers default is redacted PII, but for Dedicated/Private you can opt into full request logging with proper access controls and audit logs.
[03:24] Liam O'Connor: That leads to security — we need SOC2 and SSO. How does Redwood handle that?
[03:31] Maya Patel: Good question. We have SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC at the org/team level, and audit logs that can stream to your SIEM or to cloud storage. For Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integration for key management. We'll share the SOC2 report and SAML docs.
[03:52] Priya Sharma: Are audit logs queryable in the Console?
[03:56] Jordan Lee: Yes, you can search audit logs, filter by user/action/resource. There's also an export to CSV and an API.
[04:10] Markus Li: About billing data and cost allocation — can we map cost to our internal cost centers?
[04:15] Jordan Lee: You can tag routes with cost-centers and the Console supports breakdowns by tag. Our usage export includes route tags, model used, tokens, and cost estimates so you can run your own chargeback.
[04:30] Liam O'Connor: Show us the cost breakdown part please — how granular does it get?
[04:34] Jordan Lee: Switching to the Cost tab. Here we show cost per route, cost per model, and cost per tenant (if you're multi-tenant). For per-route, there's a per-token breakdown, plus a fixed per-request overhead we surface for certain features like tool-calling or function calls. The graph also projects monthly spend based on current 7/30/90 day windows.
[04:58] Priya Sharma: What about quantization — you mentioned model variants. How do we get recommendations?
[05:03] Jordan Lee: That's part of Redwood Optimize. In the Console we show Optimize recommendations inline: suggested quantization (e.g., q4/q8), batch size suggestions, and expected cost savings and latency impact. You can preview the recommended profile and apply to a route.
[05:20] Maya Patel: For example, the Optimize module might say switch 'pricing-chat' to q8 with batch size 8, which could save ~35% cost at a 5-10% latency increase in our internal benchmarks.
[05:35] Liam O'Connor: We care about tail latency — can Optimize respect SLOs?
[05:39] Jordan Lee: Yes, when you run Evaluate, you provide target SLOs and example prompts; Optimize will filter suggestions that exceed SLO thresholds. You can run a canary on a small percentage of traffic first.
[05:54] Markus Li: For Dedicated, do we get per-GPU utilization metrics? We want to tie spend to infra.
[06:00] Jordan Lee: Dedicated shows host-level metrics — GPU utilization, memory, queue depth, and the routing layer shows how requests were distributed across pools. You can also pin routes to pools so a route only uses reserved capacity.
[06:15] Priya Sharma: If a pool goes down, what's the fallback?
[06:18] Jordan Lee: Smart routing supports policy-based fallbacks: failover to hosted, or to a lower-cost quantized variant in another region. You can also set hard SLOs to trigger circuit-breaker style fallbacks.
[06:33] Liam O'Connor: Any limits on cross-region fallback? We have data residency concerns for EU customers.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: You can restrict routing policies by region and set data residency constraints. If a request is marked EU-only, fallbacks will only use EU-compatible deployments.
[06:50] Maya Patel: I'm going to show a recent customer example — build on the cost graph. You can click a spike and it will open the per-request samples and the route config at the time.
[06:58] Jordan Lee: Here's an example where a new prompt increased completion size — it drove costs up. We rolled it back and Optimize suggested a prompt rewrite and quantization.
[07:12] Priya Sharma: On the auth side, can we restrict who can apply Optimize changes? We need approvals.
[07:17] Jordan Lee: RBAC lets you define who can view vs who can apply changes. You can require approval workflows for route changes tying into your ticketing system.
[07:28] Liam O'Connor: Pricing question: what's the typical unit cost delta between hosted vs Dedicated? Ballpark.
[07:34] Maya Patel: Hosted is pay-as-you-go, per-token pricing. Dedicated is a reserved capacity model — lower per-token effective cost at higher commit levels. Exact numbers depend on model size, quantization, and commit. I'll send a pricing sheet after this call.
[07:50] Markus Li: For a 3-route pilot with mixed traffic, we'd want to see a cost projection per million requests. Can you export a CSV with projected spend?
[07:58] Jordan Lee: Yes — the export includes a projected spend column for given time windows and can be grouped by route. We can also run a benchmark using your sample traces to produce an accurate per-token and per-request estimate.
[08:15] Priya Sharma: About sample traces — what's the data onboarding flow? We're a little sensitive about sending full PII.
[08:20] Jordan Lee: For benchmarking you can either send anonymized traces or run an on-prem benchmarking harness for Private/Dedicated. For hosted, we have secure upload via S3 presigned links with encryption. We'll redact PII by default in hosted benchmarking runs.
[08:38] Liam O'Connor: Can we set alerts on cost-per-route thresholds?
[08:42] Jordan Lee: Yes, you can create alert rules — cost spikes, token count per minute, or latency SLO breaches. Alerts can go to Slack, PagerDuty, or email.
[08:52] Maya Patel: Demoing the Alerts builder — you choose metric, aggregation, threshold, and notification channel.
[08:59] Markus Li: If we run a pilot, will we get direct support from Redwood SE?
[09:03] Maya Patel: Absolutely. Pilot includes a dedicated SE touchpoint, weekly check-ins, and a runbook for the benchmark. Jordan will be your primary SE contact.
[09:11] Priya Sharma: Can you show the 'route tags' feature again? We want to tag by product, environment (prod/staging), and cost center.
[09:17] Jordan Lee: Sure — here under Routes, you can add tags. Tags are included in all analytics and exports. You can also set per-route retention policy and log forwarding.
[09:30] Liam O'Connor: A question on caching — we have a lot of repeated prefixes. How does Redwood handle prefix/KV caching?
[09:37] Jordan Lee: Redwood supports prefix caching and KV cache for sessions. The Console surfaces cache hit rates per route and estimated savings. You can configure TTLs and granular keys. There's a note about cache invalidation strategies in the docs.
[09:55] Priya Sharma: What's the latency advantage for cache hits?
[09:58] Jordan Lee: Cache hits can reduce token generation entirely for canned responses or reduce repeated prefix computation — depends on your prompts, but it's typically sub-10ms retrieval vs model inference.
[10:10] Liam O'Connor: Any automation for batch sizing? We have mixed latency needs per route.
[10:14] Jordan Lee: Optimize suggests batch size per route based on observed request patterns and latency SLOs. For high-throughput non-interactive routes batching yields large savings. For interactive chat you keep smaller batches and rely on caching.
[10:28] Maya Patel: I'm going to open the 'Optimize' recommendations for the pilot routes. You can see expected savings, CPU/GPU footprint change, and an estimated quality delta — we attach eval metrics from your prompts if you provide samples.
[10:44] Priya Sharma: How does Redwood quantify 'quality delta'? We care about hallucinations and factuality loss.
[10:49] Jordan Lee: We integrate evals — you can supply ground truth prompts and expected outputs; we run a regression test and produce metrics like exact match, BLEU-ish scores, and also semantic similarity. Bigger quantization steps sometimes reduce factuality; Optimize filters options that fail your acceptance criteria.
[11:09] Markus Li: For the pilot, we want to keep 99th percentile latency under 350ms and maximize cost savings. Will Optimize respect that?
[11:16] Jordan Lee: Yes — you set SLOs per route; Optimize only shows configurations that meet target SLOs or shows expected SLO breaches. You can then run a canary.
[11:30] Liam O'Connor: Can we automate rollbacks if SLOs are violated?
[11:34] Jordan Lee: You can set automated rollback policies — e.g., revert to previous model variant or fallback to hosted if latency exceeds threshold.
[11:44] Priya Sharma: About observability, can we get token-level traces tied to request IDs for debugging?
[11:49] Jordan Lee: Yes, request-level traces include token counts, timestamps per token batch, and model internal metrics if you enable verbose logging. These are access controlled.
[12:06] Maya Patel: Let's talk about billing cadence. Hosted is monthly billing based on usage, Dedicated can be monthly or annual committed. We'll include tiered discounts for larger commits.
[12:18] Liam O'Connor: Any penalty for bursting above commit on Dedicated?
[12:22] Maya Patel: We have burst windows for short spikes; sustained over-commit usage is billed at an overage rate that is still often cheaper than hosted depending on commit. We'll detail this in the sheet.
[12:34] Markus Li: For EU data, if we pin to EU region does the console still allow cross-region reporting?
[12:39] Jordan Lee: Cross-region reporting is available in the Console for org admins, but raw requests stay in region per data-residency constraints. Aggregated metrics are allowed but sensitive payloads remain regional.
[12:56] Priya Sharma: Anything on encryption at rest?
[13:00] Maya Patel: Data at rest is encrypted; for Private/Dedicated you can bring your own KMS. For hosted we manage keys but support customer managed keys for enterprise plans.
[13:12] Liam O'Connor: Ok, can we look at an example export CSV?
[13:16] Jordan Lee: Exporting now. The CSV includes timestamp, route, request_id, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, estimated_cost_usd, region, deployment_type, tags.
[13:30] Priya Sharma: That's perfect. On the projected savings row, can we see assumptions like q8 latency tradeoff?
[13:36] Jordan Lee: Yes, each recommendation includes assumed latency delta, expected token change (if we recommend prompt rewrite), and estimated monthly delta.
[13:48] Liam O'Connor: Regarding access, can we map Console roles to our SSO groups?
[13:52] Maya Patel: Yes, we support SCIM provisioning and group mapping so you can sync SSO groups to Console roles.
[14:04] Markus Li: For the pilot's benchmark, what kind of data do you need?
[14:08] Jordan Lee: Ideally a sample of 10k representative requests across the 3 routes with traffic shape (timestamps) and tags. If you can't share payloads, a stripped trace with token counts and response lengths is enough to estimate.
[14:22] Priya Sharma: Will that produce deterministic per-token cost estimates?
[14:26] Jordan Lee: It's an estimate — but with traces we run a real inference bench using compatible models and return more accurate run-time numbers.
[14:40] Liam O'Connor: Anything else on SLA? We need 99.9% with uptime and latency targets.
[14:46] Maya Patel: Enterprise plans include SLA commitments. We'll share the SLA language in the SOW.
[14:55] Priya Sharma: On legal, do you support Data Processing Agreements for GDPR?
[14:59] Maya Patel: Yes, DPA is standard for enterprise contracts. We'll route that through legal after the pricing sheet.
[15:08] Markus Li: One more quick question: in the per-route dashboard can we pin a version of the model so rollouts don't affect production?
[15:14] Jordan Lee: Yes, you can pin a model version for a route and use rollout policies to gradually shift traffic. The Console shows rollout % and allows rollback.
[15:26] Liam O'Connor: Great. Any examples of customers doing multi-tenant cost allocation?
[15:31] Maya Patel: We have case studies; many customers tag by tenant and route, then use the export for chargeback. I'll send a short case study.
[15:40] Priya Sharma: OK, let's recap to make sure we cover next steps.
[15:44] Maya Patel: Recap: We'll send pricing and Dedicated options; Jordan will share benchmark runbook and example CSV export; Aster to provide sample traces or anonymized token traces; set up pilot on Dedicated for 2 weeks; schedule technical deep dive for 2026-09-22.
[15:58] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. When can we get the SOC2?
[16:02] Maya Patel: We'll attach SOC2 and SAML docs with the pricing email by 2026-09-17.
[16:10] Priya Sharma: Who will be the day-to-day SE contact?
[16:13] Maya Patel: Jordan Lee.
[16:16] Jordan Lee: Happy to help — I'll also share a checklist for the pilot.
[16:22] Markus Li: Cool. Anything else?
[16:24] Maya Patel: No, thank you all. We'll follow up with the materials.
[16:27] Liam O'Connor: Appreciate it.
[16:30] Priya Sharma: Thanks.
[16:33] (end of meeting)

Notes on transcription: occasional mishears (e.g., 'KV cash' observed in earlier transcripts) and shorthand tokens; speaker attribution mostly correct but automated labels sometimes show first name only. The transcript is clipped to salient portions and sample timestamps every ~15-120s to mimic Fireflies export.
